questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is about how many times the time required for $90\%$ completion of the reaction?
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{100}{100-x}$.
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{100}{1} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 2$
$t_{90\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{100}{10} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 1$
Therefore, $t_{99\%} = 2 \times t_{90\%}$.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of $1.15 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. How long will $5\ \mathrm{g}$ of this reactant take to reduce to $3\ \mathrm{g}$? (Given: $\log 5 = 0.6990$, $\log 3 = 0.4771$)

For a first order reaction, the ratio of the time taken for $75\%$ completion to the time taken for $25\%$ completion is $x \times 10^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is _______. (Nearest Integer)
[Given: $\log_{10} 2 = 0.3010$, $\log_{10} 3 = 0.4771$, $\log_{10} 4 = 0.6020$]
questions.solution:
$t_{75\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{25}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(4) = \frac{2.303 \times 0.6020}{k}$
$t_{25\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{75}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(1.333) = \frac{2.303 \times 0.1249}{k}$
Ratio $= \frac{0.6020}{0.1249} \approx 4.819 = 48.19 \times 10^{-1}$.
Rounding to the nearest integer gives $48$.

questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $99.9\%$ completion is how many times the half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction?
questions.solution:
For first order reaction:
$t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{100 - x}$
$t_{99.9} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{0.1} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(10^3) = 3 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$.
Since $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k} \approx \frac{2.303 \log 2}{k} \approx 0.3 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$.
Therefore, $\frac{t_{99.9}}{t_{1/2}} = \frac{3}{0.3} = 10$.

questions.stem:
The rate constant of a first order reaction is $2.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. If the initial concentration of the reactant is $0.10\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$, the concentration of the reactant remaining after $100\ \mathrm{minutes}$ is $x \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$. The value of $x$ is ____________. (Nearest integer)
(Given: $e^{-1.2} = 0.301$)
questions.solution:
For first order reaction, $[A]_t = [A]_0 e^{-kt}$.
$k = 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$, $t = 100\ \mathrm{min} = 6000\ \mathrm{s}$.
$kt = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \times 6000 = 1.2$.
$[A]_t = 0.10 \times e^{-1.2} = 0.10 \times 0.301 = 0.0301\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}} = 3.01 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$.
Thus, $x \approx 3$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion of the reaction is $x$ times the time required for $90\%$ completion of the reaction. The value of $x$ is:

A first order reaction has a rate constant of $1.5 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. The time required for $5\ \mathrm{g}$ of this reactant to reduce to $3\ \mathrm{g}$ is _________ $\mathrm{s}$. (Round off to the nearest integer) [Given: $\log_{10} 3 = 0.4771$, $\log_{10} 5 = 0.6990$]
